cells.tense: Right now, here, you've got the pen.
cells.verb: holding many truths about a person at once
cells.place: in the place where you feel with someone
cells.ask: Say one of those things out loud — the shape you see in them, plainly, so they can hold it too — and things start to make sense around you.
cells.core: You can see all of someone at once and still be with them. The contradictions, the parts that don't fit, the thing they're not saying — none of it pulls you out of the room. You take in the whole person and you stay close anyway, which is harder than it looks and quieter than it sounds.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole of them and stay close anyway.

cells.tense: You're bracing at a future that hasn't been written.
cells.verb: seeing every version of a person at once
cells.place: in the place where you feel with someone
cells.ask: Pick one true thing about them and steer by that this week, letting the other readings sit unread — the knowing starts landing without you arguing for it.
cells.core: You're reading so much into people that you can't land on the one in front of you. Every angle, every version of what they might mean, what they might turn into — all of it arrives at once and you're already ahead of them, preparing for a person who hasn't shown up yet. The seeing is real. It's just outrunning the being-with.
cells.sheetLine: You see so many sides of them you can't sit with the one that's here.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: letting yourself know a person in full
cells.place: in the place where you feel with someone
cells.ask: Let one conversation go where it goes, without deciding first what they are — follow the current instead of charting it — and the knowing comes back accurate, easy with what it doesn't know yet.
cells.core: You've stopped taking people in whole. Somewhere back there, knowing that much about someone cost more than it gave, so now you take one reading and leave it at that — one version of them, held at arm's length. The capacity to see them fully hasn't gone anywhere. You've just stopped letting it near anyone.
cells.sheetLine: You know how to see all of someone. You've stopped letting yourself.

cells.tense: Pen down, in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: holding many truths about a person at once
cells.place: in the place where you feel with someone
cells.ask: Next time you catch yourself already knowing what someone's owed, say 'I saw that' — to yourself, once, plainly — and the knowing lands without a fight.
cells.core: You already read people in full — you hold their contradictions, you know three things about them before they've finished a sentence, and it shapes how you move with them. But you talk about it as if it just happens, or as if you're not that perceptive. The seeing is doing real work in every room you're in. You're the only one not giving it your name.
cells.sheetLine: You're already reading them whole. You just don't call it yours.
